newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade slow,thin test-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade slow,thin test-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales near midday on Friday were slow in a limited test, feedlot sources said.

About 700 heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold at $68.00 per cwt in the Texas Panhandle/ western Oklahoma area, down $1.00 from this week's active sales, they said. The sales follow a weekly movement of 89,000 head.
There were no reported sales in Kansas following weekly movement of 97,700 head, sources there said.
Most showlists were near or completely sold out after this week's early packer buying, the sources said.
The bulk of this week's cattle sold at $69.00, up $1.00 from last week amid strong packer demand to fill pre-Memorial Day orders from retailers for advertising features, they said.
Packers early in the week were aggressive buyers to ensure they had adequate supplies of high-yielding cattle, several cattle feeders said.
However, the holiday beef demand appeared to be waning as suggested by lower beef prices Wednesday and Thursday, the sources said.
